chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed ibn Uqbah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasr al-Taymi, who said: I heard Harb ibn al-Hasan al-Tahhan narrating to Yahya ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi that Yahya ibn al-Masawar said:

A group of Shia were present, and among them was Ali ibn Abi Hamza. I heard him say: Ali ibn Yaqtin entered upon Abul Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) and asked him about some matters, and he answered him. Then Abul Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ali, your companion will kill me.' Ali ibn Yaqtin began to weep and said: 'Master, am I also with him?' He said: 'No, O Ali, do not be with him and do not witness my killing.' Ali said: 'Who is for us after you, O Master?' He replied: 'This Ali, my son; he is the best of those who will succeed me. His position to me is like my position with my father; he is for my Shia, with him is the knowledge they need. He is the leader in this world and the leader in the Hereafter, and indeed he is among the亲近 ones.' Yahya ibn al-Hasan said to Harb: 'So what caused Ali ibn Abi Hamza to disassociate from him and be jealous of him?' Harb said: 'I asked Yahya ibn al-Masawar about that, and he said: What motivated him was the wealth he had taken for himself, so that Allah would make him wretched in this world and the Hereafter.'

key_terms.الْمُقَرَّبِيْنَ: The亲近 ones (those close to God)

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam Musa al-Kadhim identify as his killer among his companions, and why?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* elucidates the origins of the Waqifiyya sect by contrasting Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who remained with the Imam until his death, with Ali ibn Yaqtin, who was instructed to witness the martyrdom but did not kill him. The text highlights Ali ibn Abi Hamza’s status as a learned successor (*sayyid*) while attributing his eventual jealousy and disassociation to his retention of the Imam's wealth, a detail that Shia scholars often interpret as a test of spiritual detachment versus material attachment.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 68 - Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Saeed bin Uqbah has narrated from Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Nasr Teemi that he said:I heard Harb bin Hasan Tahan that Yahya bin Hasan Alawi has narrated a tradition that Yahya bin Masawar said:

I was present in a gathering of Shia people and Ali bin Hamza was among them. I heard him say: Ali bin Yaqtin came to Abul Hasan Musa (a.s) and posed some queries to him. The Imam gave replies to him. After that Abul Hasan (a.s) said: O Ali, your companion would kill me. Ali bin Yaqtin began to weep and said: Master, am I also with him? Imam (a.s) replied: You are not with him and you will not see me being killed. Ali said: Master, who is the Imam after you? He replied: My son, Ali is the best of those who would survive me. His position to me is like my position with my father; and he is having all the knowledge that Shia are in need of. [He is knowledgeable about every matter]. He is the chief and leader in the world and the hereafter and is from the proximate ones of the court of Almighty Allah. Yahya bin Hasan Harb said: Thus what caused Ali bin Abi Hamza to keep away from Imam Ali Ridha (a.s) and to be jealous of him? Harb replied: I asked the same thing from Yahya bin Masawar and he said: He refused to hand over to Imam Ali Ridha (a.s) that which he was having from the wealth of Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s) and that is why Almighty Allah deemed him unfortunate in the world as well as the hereafter.
